key_insight: Adding a hemispherical leading-edge curvature changes separation and vortex shedding at Re = 1000, delaying onset of unsteady shedding for some angles while strengthening near-plate vortical structures.
engineering_relevance: Leading-edge shape can be tuned to balance stability and glide performance for low-Re small UAVs or aquatic vehicles operating at different angles of attack.
method: 2D numerical simulation of a flat plate with and without hemispherical leading-edge curvature
Swept angle of attack from 0° to 25° at Reynolds number 1000
Compared vortex shedding behavior, shedding frequency, and aerodynamic force/glide-ratio response
evidence_signal: The abstract reports angle-dependent force coefficients, multiple shedding frequencies at higher angles, and different onset of shedding between the curved and simple flat plates.
watch_item: Results are from 2D simulations at a single low Reynolds number, so real 3D effects and broader operating conditions may alter the observed performance trends.
paper_title: Effect of leading edge geometry on aerodynamic performance of a flat plate
